title: Per-route Observability Retention Gating + Security Questionnaire Automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Run a controlled experiment that offers per-route observability retention levels as an add-on SKU, gated behind an entitlement and an automated security questionnaire (SQ) flow during enterprise contract onboarding. Rationale: many enterprise customers want the ability to increase retention for specific API routes (eg. model outputs for debugging/rate-limited auditing) without committing to org-wide higher retention or full premium SLA. Combining a per-route credit model with an automated SQ reduces legal friction for low-risk customers while enabling sales to upsell higher retention/SLA packages.
background: Current state: observability retention tiers are org-scoped and surfaced as a single entitlement in billing. Sales reports indicate a demand for route-level retention for debugging high-volume features (chat history, multimodal attach points) and customers are reluctant to take org-wide retention increases due to cost and data governance. Security questionnaire gating today is manual and adds 2–3 weeks to contract sign—blocking medium-sized customers from early adoption of retention add-ons.
scope:
- Backend: entitlement service changes to support per-route SKUs, token-scoped route metadata, and rate-limited observability credits.
- Billing: new pricing line item 'Per-route Observability Credits' with conversion rules.
- Console: UI to enable/assign retention per API route and surface projected monthly cost.
- Onboarding: automated SQ workflow that maps questionnaire answers to allowable retention levels; auto-approve low-risk patterns.
- E2E: experiments dashboards and metrics instrumentation to measure adoption, revenue uplift and false-positive security rejections.
acceptance_criteria: Create entitlement 'per_route_observability' and support assignment at route level in entitlement service
Console UX: route-level retention control visible in routes table and route detail, with cost estimate and toggle
Automated SQ: implement a 10-question lightweight questionnaire; responses produce an allow/deny/flag outcome for per-route retention up to 30 days
Billing: charges for per-route credits appear on invoice and usage API with clear metric names
Feature gating: rollout mechanism to enable experiment only for selected accounts/cohorts
Dashboards: metrics pipeline emits adopt_rate, avg_retention_days_per_route, revenue_delta, and support_ticket_rate for cohort analysis
metrics: Adoption rate among targeted pilot orgs (target >= 20% within 4 weeks)
Revenue uplift from add-on purchases (baseline +5% target by end of pilot)
Avg cost per customer to Redwood (infra cost delta) vs revenue delta
Time-to-approve for SQ automated vs manual (target < 48 hours for auto-approve)
Support tickets related to retention config (target: <= 10 for pilot cohort)
plan: 1) Week 0–1: finalize PRD, pricing bands and legal guardrails; obtain security review scope. 2) Week 1–3: build entitlement and billing schema; add usage metrics. 3) Week 2–4: implement console UX mocks and small frontend flow; wire to entitlement API. 4) Week 3–5: build SQ automation engine (questionnaire + rule engine) with an admin review path. 5) Week 5–6: internal dogfood and stability testing; prepare rollout cohorts. 6) Week 6–10: pilot with 10–15 selected customers (mix of scaleups and mid-market). 7) Week 10–12: analyze results and decide on GA, iterate on pricing or expand allowed retention ceilings.
rollout: Alpha: internal (Redwood platform team) — enable for 3 internal orgs
Beta: invite-only pilot for 10 customers (sales-sourced) — cohorts A/B pricing: fixed monthly add-on vs per-credit usage
Evaluation checkpoint: 6 weeks after beta start — data review with sales, legal, infra
GA gate: SLA and security review sign-off, billing integration validated, support playbook published
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: per-route retention increases flexibility but complicates billing and entitlement surface; rule-based SQ reduces manual lift but may incorrectly classify edge cases leading to compliance risk. Risks: data residency/regulatory constraints for long retention on specific routes; unexpected cost increases from customers enabling high retention on high-volume routes. Mitigations: cap maximum retention per route for pilot (30 days), alerting on infra cost anomalies, require manual legal review for flagged SQ outcomes.
dependencies: ENG-45390 (billing: line-item and invoice schema changes)
legal_considerations: Require new contract language for per-route retention that callers must accept: explicit ROI/usage commitments, caps per route, and data handling statements. Draft clause in PRD section 'contract-clause-draft'. Escalation path to legal for SQ-flagged customers.
support_playbook: Create support KB article that explains how retention credits are consumed, how to disable route retention, and troubleshooting steps. Include runbook for cost anomaly detection and rollback steps for accidental high-retention configs.
